Finding: Higher early engagement was consistently associated with lower-risk outcomes across both OULAD and KDD Cup 2015.
Evidence: Total interactions, active days, active weeks and unique resources showed the same direction of association in both cohorts.

Finding: Early engagement features provided measurable predictive discrimination in both learning cohorts.
Evidence: OULAD XGBoost AU-ROC = 0.7971; KDD XGBoost AU-ROC = 0.8542 using 10-fold cross-validation.

Finding: Temporal engagement measures were important contributors to model predictions.
Evidence: In the KDD XGBoost analysis, active_days_4w had the largest mean absolute contribution, followed by total_interactions_4w.

Finding: The direction of association between early engagement and outcomes was consistent across the two cohorts.
Evidence: All four aligned engagement features showed consistent direction across OULAD and KDD.

Finding: Predictive discrimination was retained when models were transferred between cohorts, but classification behaviour changed across cohorts.
Evidence: OULAD → KDD AU-ROC = 0.7795; KDD → OULAD AU-ROC = 0.7470. Predicted positive-rate shifts were also observed.

Finding: Predictive performance varied across demographic subgroups, indicating the importance of subgroup-level evaluation.
Evidence: Differences in FPR, FNR, precision and recall were observed across gender, age and disability groups.
